title: Skipped acquisition
description: One acquisition a chip run could not include, in the product's own words (`umbra_py.chips.SkippedAcquisition.to_dict`). It is one line of the `skipped.jsonl` sidecar written beside the manifest, and one entry of the `skipped` array in a chip dataset summary — the same record either way, so a loader reading the directory and an agent reading stdout learn the same thing. Only a *final* fact about a product produces one: metadata that cannot support the request, or no readable product behind the href. A transport failure does not, because a dropped connection says nothing about the archive.

datetime.description: When it was acquired, so a gap in a time series can be located. Null when the source item stated none.

reason.description: The refusal's own words — verbatim from the `UnsupportedMeasurementError` or `UnreadableProductError` that produced it, naming what the product does carry rather than paraphrasing what it does not.

hint.description: The single recovery step the refusal named, or null when no one step applies.

stage.description: When the hole was found, which is the one thing the two routes to it do not share. `conversion` means the product was downloaded and then refused (`--skip-unsupported`); `preflight` means its metadata was read over the wire and it was never downloaded at all (`--preflight`). The reason is the product's own either way, so only the cost differs.
